title: Provision of Affordable Meals and Other Contractual Obligations at Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centres
what_it_is: Provision of Affordable Meals and Other Contractual Obligations at Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centres

sections.label: Hawker centre cost and contract questions
sections.summary: Questions ask what principles guide who bears the cost of affordable meals for low-income patrons and whether NEA oversight of SEHC contracts will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what principles currently guide who should bear the cost of providing affordable and nutritious meals to low-income patrons; and (b) whether the Ministry will review the current distribution of responsibility for providing such meals to low-income patrons between Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centre operators, their stallholders, NEA, and consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centre operators require the approval of NEA to change contractual terms with stallholders; (b) how regularly does NEA review contracts between SEHC operators and stallholders; (c) whether NEA can and has exercised its veto against such contractual terms; and (d) whether NEA intends to conduct a comprehensive review of the SEHC model.

sections.label: NEA tenancy agreement guidelines
sections.summary: NEA has put in place basic guidelines for tenancy agreement terms since 2018 to safeguard stallholders' interests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: To safeguard the interests of stallholders, the NEA has, and since 2018, put in place basic guidelines for tenancy agreement terms.

sections.label: NEA stall rental caps
sections.summary: Since 2019 NEA has capped stall rentals to average independently-valued rents and discounted rent in a centre's first two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: Since 2019, the NEA has capped stall rentals to average independently-valued rents, as well as discounted rent in the first two years of a centre's operation as we recognise that an SEHC's footfall and operations would require time to be built up and stabilise.

sections.label: Operator removes scheme requirement
sections.summary: The operator has not implemented the scheme and, after feedback, decided to remove the requirement from new agreements and tenancy renewals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this, I understand that the operator has not implemented the scheme to-date and following feedback from stallholders and the public, the operator has decided to remove the requirement from new agreements and tenancy renewals.

sections.label: Quarterly stallholder feedback sessions
sections.summary: SEHC operators must hold quarterly feedback sessions with stallholders, attended by NEA representatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: SEHC operators are required to conduct quarterly feedback sessions with their stallholders, which are also attended by NEA representatives.

sections.label: SEHC satisfaction survey results
sections.summary: NEA surveys between 2021 and 2024 found satisfaction levels above 80% for various aspects of SEHC management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: Satisfaction levels for various aspects of SEHC management have been higher than 80% based on NEA's surveys between 2021 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: NEA has always sought to strike a balance between safeguarding the interests of both hawkers and patrons, whilst giving SEHC operators sufficient room to set requirements aligned with their business strategies to help their SEHCs thrive and succeed.

sections.label: Median rents at SEHCs
sections.summary: In 2024, median monthly rent was $1,750 at SEHCs and $1,450 at non-subsidised stalls in similar NEA-managed hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: In 2024, the median monthly rent at SEHCs, compared to non-subsidised stalls at similar NEA-managed hawker centres, were $1,750 for the former and $1,450 for the latter.

sections.label: Stallholders and value meals
sections.summary: Different stalls assemble budget meals differently, and stallholders are not expected to make a loss selling value meals.

sentences.text: As the Member has suggested, a "cai png" stall will have a very different way of putting together some ingredients to meet the budget meal price, whereas a Japanese stall or a noodle stall would have a different way of putting together a meal that is within this price.
I think it is also important for me to highlight that stallholders are not expected to make a loss when selling the value meals.

sections.label: App and publicity costs
sections.summary: Costs of apps and publicity vary across centres but are not passed on to stallholders.

sentences.text: Because these apps and different publicity efforts vary from location to location, the cost then varies across centres.
But what is clear is that these are not passed on to the stallholders.

sections.label: NEA awareness of programme
sections.summary: NEA was aware of the "Pay It Forward" programme and the requirement put into the tenancy agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: So, the first part of the first question is, was NEA aware?

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: I mentioned in my reply just now, NEA was aware of the "Pay It Forward" programme and the requirement that was put into the tenancy agreement.

sections.label: Value meals share of sales
sections.summary: Value meals account for 5% to 20% of the number of meals a hawker sells.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: An additional point is that, today, value meals account for 5% to 20% of the number of meals a hawker sells.

sections.label: Operators plough back surpluses
sections.summary: Operators are expected to plough back 50% of operating surpluses into activities that drive traffic to the centre and benefit hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, operators, for instance, are expected to plough back 50% of operating surpluses to conduct activities that drive traffic to the centre and that benefits the hawkers.

sections.label: NEA officers at tenancy signing
sections.summary: NEA officers are generally present at tenancy agreement signing to ensure terms are explained properly and understood by hawkers and stallholders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: First and foremost, NEA officers are generally there during the tenancy agreement signing to ensure that terms are explained properly and that hawkers and the stallholders themselves understand what is being communicated.

sections.label: Budget meal items on menus
sections.summary: Hawkers can sell other meal items at various price points, and are asked to come up with a budget meal item on their menu, not to subsidise it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: So, you have one at $3.00 or $3.50, and then you have the ability to sell other meal items at various price points, depending on your business strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: We are not asking the hawkers themselves to dish out a subsidy for these budget meal items.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: We are asking them to come up with an item on their menu.
